note: Work: 16. Employment Order, 2009 (S 37, gazetted 5 September 2009, made under Article 83(3) of the Constitution; read in the gazette text the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly's legal network (aipalync.org) holds, the Attorney General's Chambers' own copy answering 404 and its archive.org snapshot not fetching): s. 9(1), a person under 16 can't enter a contract of service; s. 9(2), from 16 to 18 only in an occupation the Commissioner approves as not injurious to youths (not held). A 'child' is under 15; s. 103 bars employing a child in any undertaking except a family industrial one, and lets a child of 14 do light work suited to capacity outside industry (not held). Later amendments and the revised Laws of Brunei text (Employment Act, Cap. 278) weren't compared. Performers: barred, the reading being that the Order has no exception for performers. Majority: 18. No Age of Majority Act is among the Attorney General's Chambers' BRULAW titles (read A to Z, 2026-11-03); the Interpretation and General Clauses Act (Cap. 4, 2022 revised edition), s. 2(1), which applies to every written law save where the contrary intention appears, defines an 'infant' and a 'minor' as a person who hasn't attained eighteen. Service: none. The Royal Brunei Armed Forces Act (Cap. 149, 2018 edition), s. 12, has recruiting officers enlist eligible persons of eighteen who offer to enlist (s. 14); its 'compulsory engagement' is the least term an enlisted soldier serves, not conscription; a later section opens 'Subject to the provisions of any written law provided for compulsory service', but no compulsory-service law is among BRULAW's titles. Until 2026-11-03 the majority stood null, an official copy not found (a web search of 2026-10-31 found only an unsourced site saying 18), and service null, no defence law read.
